title: Inter-Dinucleotides Selective Correlations Show Single or Double Stranded Conditions of Viruses and Interactions with Lytic or Latent Life Cycles
content: Dinucleotides whose bases are separated by o, 1, 2, … K nucleotide sites showed a huge deviation from randomness (neutral) evolution. It showed, also a periodicity of the value of the distance to randomness. Further studies revealed this study could indicate the double or single stranded condition of viruses. This is not the stranded condition found in virions, but the condition during the whole viral cycle; in replication or translation, viruses have a mixed single and double stranded behavior. This is an evolutionary vision of the viral cycle where mutation, selection or drift occur. The study intended to confirm these results, to extend them to the lytic or latent condition, and to give insight on the evolutionary and dynamic vision of single or double stranded behavior of viruses. Results confirm the great distance to neutrality, the periodicity of the distance to neutrality, the discrimination of single or double stranded condition and the evolutionary dynamic behavior of viral nucleic acids during the viral cycle. The lytic or latent property showed a great interaction with single or double stranded condition and with the DNA or RNA constitution that indicated the number of viruses was smaller than needed to study this aspect.
